title: Brutally Honest: Yeon's Reading

plan.title: What strangers clock in ten seconds
Your red flag (don't pretend you don't have one)
What you overdo, and what you dodge
How you wreck your own love life
What the group chat says when you're not in it
Friends and work: Yeon has receipts
The lie you keep telling yourself
The compliment you keep swatting away

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. Your first impression lands harder than you think. You walk in with an opinion of the room and the room can feel it.

Bom: Some people find that magnetic.

Yeon: Others decide in ten seconds you're "a lot" and sit at the other end of the table forever.

Next new-people thing: ask three curious questions before you share one opinion. You'll still make an impression. It'll just include "interested in other humans".

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You enter a room like you're about to review it.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. In the first ten seconds, people mostly see you watching them.

Yeon: Which is lovely, and also why half of them leave thinking you didn't like them. You liked them. You were just buffering.

Bom: Your warmth arrives on a delay.

Next time, say one real thing in the first minute. A compliment, a joke, an opinion. Skip the buffering.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your warmth is real. Let it arrive a few minutes earlier.

strong.text:
Built strong, so your red flag comes with its own lawyer.

Yeon: Someone points it out and you've got a rebuttal, three examples and a closing statement ready before they've finished the sentence.

Bom: You're not trying to win. You're trying not to feel caught.

Yeon: Sweet. Still a closing statement.

Next time somebody names it, say "Huh. Say more." Then stop talking for a full minute. No "to be fair".

Yeon: You don't have to agree. You just have to stop winning long enough to hear it.

Bom: And if three people from three different corners of your life have said the same thing?

Yeon: That's not everyone being sensitive. That's a pattern with witnesses.

Bom: Being told isn't being attacked. Somebody risked the awkwardness because they want to stay close to you.

Yeon: Thank them. Through gritted teeth, if needed. Gritted-teeth thanks still count.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Say "huh, say more." Then zip it for sixty seconds. Painful. Works.

weak.text:
Built soft, so your red flag wears an apology.

Yeon: "Sorry, quick question." "Sorry if that's weird." "Sorry, ignore me." You have apologised to a chair you bumped into.

Bom: You're trying so hard not to be a bother.

Yeon: And accidentally hiring everyone as your full-time reassurance department.

This week, count the sorries nobody needed. Swap half of them for thank-yous. "Thanks for waiting" lands warmer than "sorry I'm late", and you stop asking to be forgiven for existing.

Bom: Watch what's under it, too. Swallow enough small wants and they come back as one sharp sentence nobody saw coming.

Yeon: Early and plain is cheap. Late and furious costs everyone.

Bom: People can't meet your needs if they only find out about them during the explosion.

Yeon: Tiny, boring honesty on a Wednesday. Nobody ever made a film about it, and it works anyway.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Count the sorries this week. Trade half for thanks. Same manners, new spine.

strong.text:
Built strong means you don't date. You drive.

Yeon: You pick the restaurant, the holiday, the pace and the name of the hypothetical dog. They enjoyed the ride for about eight months.

Bom: Then they went quiet, and you couldn't work out why, because everything was going so well.

Yeon: Going well for the driver.

Hand over the wheel once a month. They plan the weekend, they choose the trip, and you say nothing in the car home. Not even "interesting choice".

Bom: And burn the ledger. Who planned, who paid, who said sorry first. Nobody signed up for a scorecard.

Yeon: Love is two people being generous, unevenly and a bit badly, for years. It was never meant to balance.

Bom: The people who stay with strong charts long-term are the ones who got to steer sometimes.

Yeon: So let them steer. Badly, even. Getting a bit lost together is its own kind of romance.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They pick the holiday. You pick silence on the drive home.

weak.text:
Built soft means you wreck love by vanishing into it.

Yeon: Their schedule, their friends, their playlist, their opinion of your friends. Six months in, you're a guest star in your own relationship.

Bom: It feels like closeness. It's you slowly getting smaller.

Yeon: And nobody falls harder for a supporting character.

Keep three things that are only yours. A hobby, a friend night, a Saturday morning with no one else in it. Defend them politely, every single week.

Bom: Watch for picking people who need rescuing, too. Being needed feels like a guarantee.

Yeon: It's a job. Find someone who wants you, not someone who requires you.

Bom: And if your partner has never once heard you say "actually, I'd rather not", they haven't met you yet.

Yeon: Start tiny. A film. A takeaway. Work up to the holiday.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your Saturday, your friends, your hobby. Non-negotiable. Say it nicely.

strong.text:
Receipt for strong charts: you redo other people's work because yours is the correct version.

Yeon: Efficient. It also teaches the whole team that their bit gets overwritten anyway, so why try. Then you complain you do everything.

Bom: You just care that it's good.

Yeon: Care quieter.

With friends you hand out advice generously and almost never on request. New rule: before any take, ask "Do you want my opinion, or do you want to vent?" Then respect the answer, even when it physically hurts.

Bom: You're incredible in a crisis.

Yeon: And you ghost the boring middle. You rescue the project at 11pm and skip the follow-up meeting. Stay for one dull follow-up this month. That's where respect turns into trust.

Bom: People would follow you anywhere.

Yeon: They'd follow you even further if you occasionally asked where they wanted to go.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "Opinion or vent?" Ask first. Then obey the answer.

weak.text:
Receipt for soft charts: you're the yes at work, and then you're the one still there at seven, doing the yes.

Yeon: Liked, useful, and mysteriously invisible at review time, because you never mentioned any of it.

Bom: You think good work should speak for itself.

Yeon: Work can't talk, babe. Send the email.

One short message this month: what you finished and how it went. No apology in the first line.

Bom: With friends, you're the listener who never asks for anything back.

Yeon: Then one day you're sad and nobody knows how to look after you, because you never let them practise. Ask one friend for one small favour. And invite people to the fun stuff first. Right now you're everyone's emergency contact and nobody's plus-one.

Bom: You've been useful to everyone for years.

Yeon: Useful and valued are different things. Make people see the difference, starting with you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tell your boss what you finished. Ask a friend for a favour. Both awkward. Both work.

strong.text:
Bonus lie for strong charts: "I don't need anyone."

Yeon: You say it with a straight face. Your straight face is lying.

Bom: You need people who'll tell you the truth, people who'll cheer, and people who'll just sit there when the tough act runs out.

Yeon: It always runs out. Usually on a Sunday night.

And a sneaky second one: "I'm only saying it because I care." Sometimes true. Sometimes it's irritation with a nicer haircut.

Quick test before the next blunt truth: is it useful to them right now, and would you say it like that to your boss? Two noes, hold it. The truth keeps.

Bom: You'd never say it, but you'd love someone to look after you for once.

Yeon: Just once. Without having to be ill first.

Bom: Needing people doesn't make you smaller.

Yeon: It makes you normal, which I know is the real insult. Next chapter, someone says something nice about you, and I already know you'll dodge it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Useful now? Fine to say to your boss? If not, it waits.

weak.text:
Bonus lie for soft charts: "I don't mind."

Yeon: You mind. The restaurant, the plan, the way they spoke to you on Tuesday. You mind in high definition.

Bom: You just don't want to be a burden.

Yeon: The minding doesn't leave. It gets filed, and it comes back three weeks later as exhaustion or one weirdly sharp comment about the dishes.

Practise minding small things out loud. "I'd prefer the other place." "That joke stung a bit." Plain voice, no apology, low stakes. Every time nothing explodes, the lie loses a little grip.

Bom: You've spent so long being easy that being honest feels rude.

Yeon: Honest isn't rude. Honest is information. People can't love what they've never been told.

Bom: And the quieter lie under it: "They're better off without me bothering them."

Yeon: You tell yourself that right before you go silent. It's almost never true. Speaking of things you refuse to believe, next chapter is a compliment. Brace.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You do mind. Say so, small and early. Nothing explodes. Promise.

strong.text:
Bom's extra for strong charts. Yeon is reading it out under protest.

Yeon: One soft habit, every day, for two weeks. Something you'd normally call pointless.

Bom: Ask about someone's weekend and listen to the whole answer. Send a thank-you for a tiny thing. Admit you were wrong about something minor, out loud, with a witness.

Yeon: The witness matters. Otherwise you'll deny it later.

Strong charts change through reps, not revelations. You already know the insight. You've already argued with it. The habit makes your strength easier to stand next to, so more people let you lead.

Bom: Then once a month, ask one person how you've been to deal with lately. Really ask.

Yeon: Someone with permission to say "you've been a bit much" is worth more than this whole comic. Don't tell Bom I said that.

Bom: And notice who relaxes around you as you soften. That's your proof.

Yeon: Write their names down. You'll want evidence the next time softness looks like weakness.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One soft habit a day for two weeks. Yeon calls it winning. I call it you, softer.

weak.text:
Bom's extra for soft charts. Yeon signed off on it, which never happens.

Bom: One brave habit a day for two weeks. Tiny, but it has to take up space.

Yeon: Speak first in one meeting a week. Pick the restaurant every single time someone asks. Send the text you've been drafting for three days without rereading it nine times.

Bom: You change through evidence. You need to see, over and over, that taking up room doesn't cost you the people you love.

Yeon: Mostly it does the opposite. They relax, because finally somebody knows what you want.

Keep a tiny list. Every time you took up space and it went fine, write it down. Soft charts forget the proof and remember the fear. Reread it on wobbly days.

Bom: You don't have to become loud. You just have to become findable.

Yeon: Findable is plenty. Loud is my job.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One brave little thing a day. People finally get to meet you.

peer_strong.text:
Your chart is stacked with {dm_el}, your own element. Picture a room full of you.

Yeon: Which explains the competing. Who's busiest, who's most tired, who had the worst commute. Nobody else knew it was a contest.

Bom: You'd rather struggle alone than owe anyone.

Yeon: And you keep a secret tally of who helped who. It's not secret. We can all see it.

The brutal bit: people stop offering help, because you made it very clear you'd rather do it yourself. Accept the next offer, even when you'd be faster. The task isn't the point. Letting someone in is.

Bom: You give the best advice in the group.

Yeon: And take none. Take one piece this month. (Saju calls this the peer family: siblings, rivals, mirrors.)

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A room full of you. Stop racing your friends to be the most tired.

output_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the stuff your {dm_el} pours out: jokes, talent, takes. (Saju calls it the output family.)

Yeon: So you're the funniest person in the group chat, and the one most likely to send the line everyone regrets laughing at.

Bom: You're genuinely talented.

Yeon: Talented, and allergic to rules. Your boss, your landlord, a sign that says please don't. You poke all of them for sport.

Pick one place where the sharp line stays in your head. Work meetings or family dinners, your choice. Notice how much smoother the week goes when not every thought gets published.

Bom: You're charming enough to get away with a lot.

Yeon: Which is exactly why you shouldn't test it daily.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: hilarious, sharp, anti-rules. Keep the filter on somewhere. Anywhere.

wealth_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} grabs and manages. (Saju calls it the wealth family. It means what you go after.)

Yeon: You're the operator. Group trip spreadsheet, colour-coded. A schedule for a picnic.

Bom: You get things done. People rely on that.

Yeon: People also feel managed. Even when you're being helpful. Especially then.

Your partner doesn't want a project manager. Your friends don't want a quarterly review of their dating life. Let one thing this week be run badly by somebody else and keep your hands in your pockets.

Bom: Some of the control is worry in a blazer.

Yeon: If letting go feels impossible, ask what you think happens if you do. The answer is usually smaller than the fear.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: you run everything. Let one thing get run badly. Hands in pockets.

power_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that keeps your {dm_el} in line. Rules, duty, status, an inner boss who never clocks off. (Saju's power family.)

Bom: You're disciplined. You actually care what's right.

Yeon: And you judge. Quietly, constantly. Yourself first, everyone else a close second.

Bom: People trust your standards.

Yeon: People also hide their drafts from you.

One appreciation for every correction, out loud. That's the whole fix, and it's why people keep bringing you their work instead of tucking it away.

Bom: The person you're hardest on is you.

Yeon: Lower your own bar first. Everyone around you gets the trickle-down.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: a judge with no off switch. One compliment per correction.

resource_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}: learning, comfort, being looked after. (Saju's resource family.)

Yeon: You've researched the gym, the course and the move for months. You've done none of them.

Bom: You're thoughtful. You like to be ready.

Yeon: You've been ready since March. Your sofa has seen more of your ambition than any human.

Pick one thing you've been reading about and start it badly this week. Not after one more video. Today, badly, in the wrong shoes.

Bom: You'd be a wonderful teacher.

Yeon: If you ever finished the course.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: forty tabs of research, zero starts. Start badly. Today.

output_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} gives out: entertaining, performing, keeping everyone's mood up. On a soft chart, that drains you.

Yeon: You're the life of the party who gets home, lies on the floor and stares at the ceiling for forty minutes.

Bom: You make everyone feel good.

Yeon: You're performing likeable. Nobody hired you for that.

Next gathering, stay quiet for the first hour. Let someone else carry the conversation. The people who still come and find you are your people.

Bom: Anyone who only wants the fun version of you isn't really a friend.

Yeon: That's an audience. Audiences don't help you move flats.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: the entertainer who goes home empty. Be boring for an hour. See who stays.

wealth_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} tries to hold and manage. Old saju books have a phrase for it: too much to carry, not enough behind you.

Yeon: Translation: other people's problems, other people's moods and other people's deadlines, all in your tote bag.

Bom: You just want everyone to be okay.

Yeon: Nobody gave you that job. You took it, unpaid, on no sleep.

Every time you say yes to carrying something for someone, ask what you're putting down to make room. Usually it's sleep, or your own plans. Put down one thing this week that was never yours.

Bom: You can love people without holding all their stuff.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: everyone's bags, your arms. Drop one. It was never yours.

power_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that pressures your {dm_el}. On a soft chart it feels like being marked all day long.

Yeon: You reread your emails for tone. You replay conversations in the shower. You rehearse ordering coffee.

Bom: You're only trying to get it right.

Yeon: You almost never got it wrong. The critic in your head is loud, not accurate.

Next time it starts, ask it for evidence. Facts, not feelings. It usually has none. Then do the thing anyway, with the critic grumbling in the back seat.

Bom: Nobody is grading you as hard as you are.

Yeon: Everyone else is busy panicking about their own grades.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: an inner critic with zero receipts. Ask for evidence. Watch it stall.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Yeon: Translation: you look tougher than you feel.

Bom: People assume you're fine because everything looks full. And you play along, because a wobble feels embarrassing.

Yeon: Then you fall apart privately, in the car, to a sad playlist.

Drop the tough act around people who'd happily help. Tell one person you're not okay before it turns into a crisis. Needing backup is the normal kind of strong.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You look solid. You feel shaky. Tell one person before it's a crisis.

output_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the outlet: saying how you feel.

Yeon: So you feel everything and say nothing, for weeks, and then you say all of it at once. About the dishwasher.

Bom: People think you're calm.

Yeon: Calm like a kettle.

Smaller vents, more often. "That annoyed me" on the day beats a monologue in a month.

Bom: That kettle is running your love life too. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: silent for weeks, then a TED talk about the dishwasher. Vent small.

wealth_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's follow-through: chasing a thing all the way to the finish.

Yeon: Big starts. Brilliant ideas. A graveyard of projects at ninety percent.

Bom: You love the beginning of things.

Yeon: Which, coincidentally, is also how you date.

Pick one project and finish the boring last bit. Show someone the finished thing. Finished beats brilliant.

Yeon: Now, about loving beginnings. Next page is your love life. Sit down.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: twelve projects at ninety percent. Finish one. Show it off.

power_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the element of limits and outside rules.

Yeon: You make your own rules, change them when convenient, and act genuinely shocked when people expect you on time.

Bom: You're free. That's lovely.

Yeon: Free is lovely until your friend has been waiting outside the restaurant for twenty-five minutes.

Borrow some structure. A calendar you actually open. A friend allowed to say "you said you'd do this." Turning up on time is affection people can see.

Bom: Partners notice who turns up. Which brings us to love.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: rules are optional, apparently. Get a calendar. Open it.

resource_strong.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's rest and being looked after.

Yeon: You run on fumes and pride. You'd pull an all-nighter before you'd ask for help.

Bom: You're so capable.

Yeon: That isn't toughness. It's bad planning in a leather jacket.

Sleep. Say yes when someone offers food. Let a person carry something for you.

Bom: Letting people look after you is a skill, and it matters most in love. Which is exactly where we're going next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: fumes, pride and a fourth coffee. Let someone feed you.

output_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's expression. On a soft chart, its absence saves your battery.

Yeon: It also means your opinions are classified. Meetings, friendships, dates. Nobody knows what you think.

Bom: You think a lot, though. And it's good.

Yeon: Then leak some. One opinion a day, out loud. Even "I don't love this song" counts.

Bom: Your opinion belongs in the room. Especially the next room we're walking into: your love life.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: your opinions are top secret. Declassify one a day.

wealth_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's going after things.

Yeon: You wait to be offered. The job, the date, the last slice. Sometimes it comes. Often somebody louder grabs it first.

Bom: You don't want to seem pushy.

Yeon: Asking isn't pushy. Asking is asking.

This week, ask for one thing you'd normally wait to be handed.

Bom: Hold that thought. Waiting to be chosen shows up in love too, and that's next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you queue politely while louder people get served. Ask.

power_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's outside pressure.

Bom: Good news: fewer bosses living in your head.

Yeon: Bad news: without a deadline you drift. The thing you care about has been "next month" since spring.

Set one gentle deadline and tell someone. Not to pressure you. To remind you it matters.

Yeon: Drifting has a love version too. Turn the page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: nobody's chasing you, so you float. One deadline. Tell a friend.

resource_weak.text:
No {miss_el} in your visible chart. For your {dm_el}, that's the element that feeds you.

Yeon: Which explains why approval feels like oxygen. A thumbs-up from the wrong person can make your whole day.

Bom: It's a gap, not a flaw.

Fill it on purpose. Kind people, real rest, learning something only for you. Then approval goes back to being a nice extra instead of a survival need.

Bom: You're allowed kindness you didn't earn.

Yeon: Now watch how that hunger runs your dating. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: that's why approval feels like air. Get your air from better places.

none_strong.text:
All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars.

Yeon: Translation: you own every tool in the box and use the hammer every time.

Bom: You could be patient. Playful. Diplomatic.

Yeon: You pick blunt because it's fastest.

Try a different tool once a day. You'll be annoyed how often it works better.

Yeon: The hammer has a favourite target, by the way. Your love life. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Five elements, one hammer. Diplomacy is in there somewhere. Find it.

none_weak.text:
All five elements show up somewhere in your pillars.

Yeon: Translation: you're more capable than you act. You can be firm, funny, clear.

Bom: And you keep choosing polite. Every single time.

Yeon: Polite is the beige of personalities.

Pick the brave option once this week. It'll go fine. Then do it again.

Bom: And notice where polite costs you most. Spoiler: love. That's the next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: All five tools, and you keep reaching for "polite". Try brave. Once.

resource.title: What refuels you: {helper_el}
resource.text:
Every chart has an element that rebalances it. For a soft {dm_el} chart, it's {helper_el}, the one that feeds you.

Yeon: Translation: you don't need more grit. You need a full tank.

Bom: Most of what's in this reading gets quieter when you're looked after. Fed people don't have to people-please, overwork or hide.

Yeon: So before you fix a single flaw, check the fuel gauge. Half of them vanish after a week of proper sleep and someone being nice to you.

Bom: Rest first, then the brave stuff. In that order.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your refill is {helper_el}. Less grit. More fuel. I mean it.

peer.title: What steadies you: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text:
Your chart already has plenty of support on paper, so the fix is more of your own element, {helper_el}. Saju reads that as peers: people at your level.

Yeon: Translation: stop collecting advice. Collect allies.

Bom: People who'll tell you the truth, then stand next to you while you act on it.

Yeon: You don't need another podcast. You need a friend with a spine. Find one who's honest and one who cheers. Bonus points if it's the same person.

Bom: People walking the same road as you, not lecturing from the end of it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: {helper_el} steadies you. Fewer podcasts. More friends with spines.

output.title: Where your extra strength should go: {helper_el}
output.text:
A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and yours is {helper_el}, the element you naturally give out.

Yeon: Translation: bossy, stubborn and judgy are what strength does when it's bored.

Bom: So give it work. Make something, teach something, move your body. Put the force where it helps.

Yeon: Next time you catch yourself bossing someone around, ask what you're not doing with your own day. Then go do that. A strong chart with a project is a joy. A strong chart without one starts running the office fridge rota.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your outlet is {helper_el}. Bored strength gets bossy. Give it a job.

wealth.title: What grounds you: {helper_el}
wealth.text:
Your chart is strong and already loud, so the fix is {helper_el}, the element you shape and work with.

Yeon: Translation: less talking, more finishing.

Bom: Opinions and drive, you've got in bulk. What calms you is something real with a deadline and a result you can point at.

Yeon: Caught yourself lecturing? Ask what you could finish today. Go finish it. Lecture later, if you still want to.

Bom: Finished things calm you more than winning arguments ever did.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: {helper_el} grounds you. Talk less. Finish more. Point at it.

wood.text:
In real life, {helper_el} means growing. Learn something, plant something, take the long walk.

Yeon: Nobody has time to be petty in the middle of a growth spurt. Which brings us to the story you keep telling yourself instead. Next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Wood fix: learn one new thing. Nobody's petty mid-growth spurt.

fire.text:
In real life, {helper_el} means warmth and being seen. Daylight, laughing, friends who light up when you walk in, saying the thing out loud.

Bom: Warm people rarely need to be defensive.

Yeon: Speaking of defensive. Next chapter is the lie you keep telling yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fire fix: daylight, and people who are glad you came.

earth.text:
In real life, {helper_el} means routine. Proper meals, a bedtime, a home that's tidy-ish, plans you actually keep.

Yeon: Boring structure underneath, and your best bits get steadier on top. Annoying, but true. Now, the story you tell yourself. You know the one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Earth fix: eat, sleep, repeat. Boring wins. I hate it too.

metal.text:
In real life, {helper_el} means edges. Decisions, decluttering, a clean no, finishing what you started.

Yeon: Clear the junk and there's room for what matters. Next up, the biggest piece of junk you're still carrying around: a lie.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal fix: empty the junk drawer. Then your calendar's junk drawer.

water.text:
In real life, {helper_el} means rest and quiet. Sleep, a swim, journaling, an evening with zero plans.

Yeon: Most bad decisions are tired decisions. And the most tired one you make is believing what's in the next chapter.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Water fix: go to bed. Nothing smart was ever decided at 2am.

rat.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Rat, 子, deep-winter Water.

Yeon: Charming at midnight, cagey by breakfast. You flirt brilliantly and open up about as fast as a bank vault.

Bom: Partners meet the charm and then the wall, and wonder which one is you.

Yeon: Both. Pick one person and hand over the code.

Rat is also a charm branch, peach blossom in saju. People drift toward you without you trying, which is how your phone fills up with almost-somethings.

Yeon: Charm opens doors. You still choose which one to walk through. Meanwhile, the group chat has opinions about you. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat at home: dazzling at midnight, locked by morning. Give one person the code.

ox.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth with Metal stored inside.

Yeon: Loyal to the point of stubborn. Once you decide how home works, that's how home works. Forever.

Bom: You make a home feel safe.

Yeon: They suggested moving the sofa in 2022. You're still considering it.

Ox is a storehouse branch. You store things: hopes, grudges, receipts, the exact words from that fight. Deep, and hard to read.

Bom: Empty the storehouse now and then, out loud, with the person it's about.

Yeon: Or the group chat will do it for you. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox at home: it's been two years. Move the sofa.

tiger.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire inside.

Yeon: Passionate, protective, restless. You love hard and then get twitchy the minute it feels like routine.

Bom: Partners get the best adventures of their lives.

Yeon: And the occasional disappearing act. Announce the twitch before you act on it.

Tiger is a travel branch, the moving horse in saju. You call it needing space. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it's boredom with a passport.

Yeon: Know which before you book the flight. Your friends have a theory, by the way. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger at home: big adventures, surprise vanishings. Say "I'm twitchy" first.

rabbit.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure spring Wood.

Yeon: Soft, stylish, allergic to conflict. You'd repaint the bedroom to avoid one awkward talk.

Bom: The home is beautiful.

Yeon: The talk is still waiting by the door. Have it before the cushions multiply again.

Rabbit is a charm branch, peach blossom in saju. People like you before you've said much, so you rarely have to fight for affection. Maybe that's why fighting for anything feels so foreign.

Bom: Your friends have noticed that too. Gently. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rabbit at home: you bought cushions instead of having the talk. Have the talk.

dragon.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp spring Earth.

Yeon: Big dreams, big pride, and big expectations you have never once said out loud.

Bom: You want something beautiful with someone.

Yeon: And they're failing a test they don't know they're sitting. Hand them the syllabus.

Dragon is a storehouse branch: you keep hopes and hurts tucked away until the shelf collapses.

Bom: Say what you hope for while it's still small enough to hear.

Yeon: Your group chat already knows what you hope for. They have screenshots. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon at home: they're sitting an exam with no syllabus. Hand it over.

snake.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Snake, 巳, early-summer Fire with Metal inside.

Yeon: You notice everything, reveal nothing and remember all of it. They think the March fight is finished. You have a folder.

Bom: You're so perceptive.

Yeon: Perceptive, with archives. Bring it up when it happens, or drop it properly.

Snake is a travel branch in saju: restless underneath, even when you look perfectly still.

Bom: Tell them when you feel itchy, instead of going cool.

Yeon: Speaking of folders, the group chat keeps one on you. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Snake at home: there's a folder from March. Raise it or shred it.

horse.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire.

Yeon: All heart, no brakes. You fall fast, love loud and bolt the second you feel fenced in.

Bom: Being loved by you feels like summer.

Yeon: Summer, with whiplash. Slow down at the start. Stay longer in the middle. The middle is where the good stuff lives.

Horse is a charm branch, peach blossom in saju: easy to fall for, hard to pin down.

Yeon: Your friends have bets on how long the next one lasts. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse at home: fast start, early exit. Stay for the middle bit.

goat.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth with Wood stored inside.

Bom: You look after everyone at home. Meals, plans, moods.

Yeon: Then you express your own needs exclusively through sighs. Long, meaningful, operatic sighs.

Bom: You don't want to ask for much.

Yeon: Your partner isn't a sigh interpreter. Words, please.

Goat is a storehouse branch: worries go in, and nothing comes out until it overflows.

Yeon: The group chat, meanwhile, hears everything. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Goat at home: a sigh is not a sentence. Use the sentence.

monkey.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Monkey, 申, early-autumn Metal with Water.

Yeon: Funniest person in the relationship. Fastest to dodge a serious talk. It gets real, you do a bit.

Bom: The bits are really good.

Yeon: The relationship still needs one unfunny Tuesday. Give it one.

Monkey is a travel branch: you keep moving so nothing heavy can land.

Bom: Let one heavy thing land. You'll survive it.

Yeon: Your friends get the bits too. They'd like the Tuesday version now and then. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey at home: one serious Tuesday. No bits. You can do it.

rooster.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Rooster, 酉, pure autumn Metal.

Yeon: Stylish, sharp, and running quality control at home. Towels folded wrong, a typo in their text. You notice, and you mention it.

Bom: You just want things to be nice.

Yeon: And your partner starts to feel like a first draft. Let one imperfection slide a day. On purpose.

Rooster is a charm branch, peach blossom in saju: people are drawn in by the polish. Let them see the unedited version too.

Yeon: The group chat has seen it. They loved it. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rooster at home: your partner is not a draft. Let one thing go today.

dog.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth with Fire stored inside.

Yeon: Loyal guard dog. Suspicious of strangers. Partners serve about a year of probation.

Bom: Once they're in, you'd fight anyone for them.

Yeon: Shorten the probation. Good people get tired of waiting at the gate.

Dog is a storehouse branch: you keep a memory of every slight and every kindness, with equal care.

Bom: Tell people about the kindness part. They never know.

Yeon: Your friends passed probation years ago and still feel watched. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog at home: a year's probation is a lot. Try six months.

pig.text:
The animal of your birth day shows how you act once love moves in. (Saju calls it the spouse palace.) Yours is the Pig, 亥, early-winter Water with Wood.

Yeon: Generous, romantic, and world champion at excusing behaviour. They forgot your birthday, but they were stressed. They cancelled again, but it's a lot right now.

Bom: You see the best in people.

Yeon: Seeing the best is lovely. A free pass every time is a welcome mat with good manners.

Pig is a travel branch: part of you is always halfway out the door, dreaming. Come back and say what you need.

Yeon: Your group chat has said it for you, by the way. Several times. Next page.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pig at home: you've excused it four times. That's a pattern, not a phase.

day_branch_heading: Who you are at home: the {day_animal} ({day_branch})

gentle.speaker: bom
gentle.text: You asked for gentle-ish. I'll hold your hand. She won't. Breathe.

honest.speaker: yeon
honest.text: Honest, like a good friend. So, the friend who tells you there's spinach in your teeth. Before the date.

savage.speaker: yeon
savage.text: "Don't hold back." You're going to regret typing that. I'm not going to regret anything.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You didn't pick a level. So you get my default. Bom is already apologising in advance.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

gye-water.first-impression:
First ten seconds: soft, quiet, watching. People sense something interesting and can't name it.

Yeon: Also, you leave parties without saying goodbye. Every time. It's a brand now.

Bom: You make people feel calm. It's like being near water.

Yeon: Calm, and slightly unsure if you liked them. You did. Tell them.
gye-water.your-red-flag:
Bom: You hate making a scene.

Yeon: So you make an absence. Same scene, worse ending.

They say something careless. You smile, go home, and slowly stop replying. Three weeks later they realise you've gone, and have no idea why.

Bom: You think saying it will make it worse.

Yeon: Saying it is the only way it gets better. "That hurt, can we talk?" Five words. Cheaper than losing a friend.
gye-water.how-you-sabotage-love:
In love you know them better than they know themselves. Every mood, every shift, every lie.

Yeon: And they know nothing about you. Not one real fear. Not one real wish.

Bom: You're just private.

Yeon: Private enough that they feel like they're dating a lovely mist.

You also decide what they're feeling without asking. You get hurt by your guess, and they don't even know there was a guess.

Bom: Ask. "Are you annoyed with me?" Four seconds.

Yeon: Saves four weeks of silent spiralling. And let them ask you. Then actually answer.
gye-water.friends-and-work:
At work you're the quiet one who notices everything. Who's stressed, who's leaving, who's lying in the meeting.

Yeon: You also never tell anyone what you think until it's too late.

Bom: You're incredibly perceptive.

Yeon: Perceptive and invisible. Your best insights die in your notes app.

With friends you're the one people tell their secrets to. You never share yours.

Bom: People feel safe with you.

Yeon: Make it two-way. Tell one friend something real this week. Unprompted.
gye-water.the-lie:
You tell yourself you're just a quiet person.

Yeon: You wrote a three-page note on your phone about how a friend made you feel. Then sent them "haha ok."

Bom: You are thoughtful.

Yeon: And hiding. You show the world a trailer and wonder why nobody's seen the film.

The truth: being seen feels dangerous. If they knew everything, they might leave. So you leave first, quietly, without saying goodbye.

Bom: You're worth knowing, Gye.

Yeon: Show one person the full film. See if they stay. They usually do.
gye-water.the-fix:
The fix, Rain. Quietly.

Yeon: Say goodbye when you leave. Every time.

Bom: Check before you conclude. One question, then listen.

Yeon: Share one real thing a week. Feelings, plans, opinions.

In love, let them see you. Not just the calm. The whole storm.

Bom: Your gentleness is precious, Gye.

Yeon: Now let people find you. Rain is lovely. A forecast would help.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: Gye. You know everyone's secrets. Nobody knows your middle name.

gye-water.speaker: bom
gye-water.text: You sense what people need before they do. That's a quiet superpower.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: You can tell who's lying in a group chat from the punctuation alone.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: Vanishing is a sentence too, Rain. Just a crueller one.

gye-water.speaker: bom
gye-water.text: Let them know one real thing about you, Gye. Mist is lovely. People prefer a hand.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: Your best ideas are in your notes app, Rain. Say one out loud in the meeting.

spring.intro: Spring rain. You feed everything around you without anyone noticing it was you. You sense moods, fix vibes, water other people's plants. Quietly essential. Quietly forgotten. Not anymore.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Everything grows a little when you're around.

summer.intro: Rain in summer, gone the moment it lands. You chase what you want in quiet, clever ways, and you vanish when a room gets too loud. People find you fascinating. They also never quite know where you went.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You left the party without saying bye. Again. Iconic.

autumn.intro: Autumn rain, fed by cool clean air. Intuitive to the point of spooky. You know who's lying, who's sad, and who's about to text before your phone even lights up.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your gut is right more often than your decisions are.

winter.intro: Winter rain. Double water. Still, deep, mostly internal. You feel everything at full volume and show about four percent of it. Your notes app has more emotional range than most novels.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your quiet isn't empty. It's full.

earth.intro: Rain falling on hard ground. Born in the soil weeks, so you met walls early: rules, expectations, people who didn't get you. You learned to soak in slowly instead of crashing through. Patient. Persistent. Underrated.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You don't fight walls. You just wear them down. Over years.

gye-water.strong:
Built strong, Gye. Intuition so well fed you think you're psychic. You're often right, which makes it worse.

Yeon: You decide what people feel without asking. You act on the read, get hurt by the read, and nobody else knew there was a read.

Bom: Your intuition really is good.

Yeon: Partners get blamed for subtext they never wrote. Friends get dropped for things they never did.

Check your read with one question before you act on it.

Bom: You're very wise.

Yeon: Wise people still check their facts.
gye-water.weak:
Built soft, Gye. Gentle rain with nowhere to land, so you soak up everyone's mood and forget your own.

Yeon: You leave a party carrying three people's sadness and none of your own joy.

Bom: You're so empathetic.

Yeon: Empathetic to the point of being a sponge. You need to wring out sometimes.

Protect one evening a week for yourself. No people, no problems.

Bom: Rain falls for others. It can pool for you too, Gye.

group-chat.text:
You're the ghost of the group chat, Gye. You read everything. You know all the drama. You say almost nothing.

Yeon: Then you send one message so perfectly observed that the whole chat goes silent for a minute.

Bom: You see everyone so clearly.

Yeon: And nobody sees you. Because you never show up in the chat.

Share one thing about your own life this week. Not a reaction to someone else's. Yours.

Bom: People want to know you.

Yeon: Your coworkers wonder about you too. Next chapter.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Read everything. Said nothing. One devastating message a month. Rain, we see you lurking.

compliment.text:
The compliment you dodge, Gye: that you're interesting.

Bom: People call you sweet, quiet, kind. You accept those. Someone says interesting and you blush and change the subject.

Yeon: Because you think you're background. A nice extra in someone else's film.

You have strange, fascinating thoughts. You notice what nobody notices. You have opinions on everything, just hidden.

Bom: You're one of the most interesting people anyone's met.

Yeon: They just haven't heard you talk yet.

Bom: Believe it. Then the final chapter. Yeon has a fix, and it's quiet.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're interesting, Gye. Very. Let people hear it.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Rain is about to quietly slip out of this compliment.

ranking.heading: Your worst habits, ranked
ranking.text:
Third place: replying to a heartfelt message with one emoji, three days later.

Second place: knowing exactly how someone feels and pretending you don't.

First place: deciding what people think of you without asking them.

Yeon: Fix for all three: ask before you assume. And reply before the weekend.

Bom: Next, what your chart is heavy with, and what it lacks.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gye's number one: reading minds, then acting on the reading. Without checking.

seven-days.heading: Seven days, seven small dares
seven-days.text:
Monday: say goodbye before leaving something.

Tuesday: share one opinion in the group chat.

Wednesday: ask someone "are we okay?" instead of guessing.

Thursday: tell a friend something real about your week.

Friday: say what you want for dinner. First.

Saturday: spend time with someone who makes you laugh.

Sunday: notice who reached for you. They were always there.

Yeon: Then reread the red flag chapter. Count the disappearances you skipped.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Day one: say bye before you leave, Gye. Whole word. Out loud.

three-people.heading: What three people would say about you, if they were brave enough
three-people.text:
Your ex: "Knew exactly how I felt. Never once told me how they felt."

Your coworker: "Quiet. Then says one sentence that changes everything."

Your best friend: "Feels everything. Says 'I'm good' with a face that is not good."

Yeon: All three love you. All three would like the four percent you show bumped to forty.

work-persona.heading: You, in a meeting
work-persona.text:
Says nothing for an hour. Then one sentence that reframes the whole problem. Everyone turns to look. You wish you hadn't spoken.

Yeon: Speak earlier. Next chapter: the blind spot that keeps you hidden.

gye-water.title: Your notes app is a novel. Your texts say "haha ok".
gye-water.text:
You're the rain. Quiet, intuitive, a little mysterious. You read people like you've seen the script.

Bom: People feel understood around you.

Yeon: People feel understood. You feel unknown. And you set it up that way.
gye-water.end: Yeon: Next page: the first impression. "Quiet." "Deep." "Wait, did they leave?"

cliff.gye-water: Yeon: Your red flag, Rain: you disappear instead of saying | you're upset. People don't know they hurt you. They just know you're gone.

gye-water.speaker: yeon
gye-water.text: Your favourite fib: "I'm just private." You're not private. You're hiding with good manners.
